Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a Java agent JAR attached to any Java 8+ application injects bytecode to capture telemetry from many popular libraries and frameworks.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: opentelemetry-bootstrap installs instrumentation for the libraries present and opentelemetry-instrument runs the app with it, configured by environment variables such as OTEL_SERVICE_NAME; Django and Flask are auto-instrumented.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: propagated context lets the called service create spans in the same trace; the default propagator uses the W3C TraceContext traceparent header.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: the stable HTTP span attributes http.request.method, url.path and http.route; span names use the low-cardinality http.route, never the raw URI path.

The company, the services, the backends and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You lead observability at Tinderbox Games, a fictional online game store. Last Black Friday a checkout slowdown took four hours to find because each service logged differently and nothing linked them. Twelve services, in Java, Python and Go, need instrumenting before this year's peak, six weeks away.
handover: Eight services are Java or Python on common frameworks; two Go services and two in-house C++ services are not.
Dashboards are built per team with their own attribute names.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

choices.feedback: Without propagated context, the gateway's spans sit in separate traces nobody can link to the slow checkout.

semconvPrompt.title: Each team names attributes its own way
semconvPrompt.context: Teams use url, httpPath, route and endpoint for the same thing.

choices.label: Adopt the semantic conventions (http.request.method, url.path, http.route, db.system and the like) for all manual spans, and build shared dashboards on them
choices.feedback: Agents already emit the conventions; manual spans that match them make every dashboard and query work across services.

choices.label: Keep team names and maintain a mapping table in the dashboards
choices.feedback: It works until the table is out of date.

choices.label: Invent a company-wide naming scheme different from the conventions
choices.feedback: The agents still emit the standard names, so every service now has two vocabularies and queries miss half the data.

scoring.modelReasoning: Zero-code agents give broad, cheap coverage of frameworks, HTTP clients and drivers; manual instrumentation through the API covers business logic agents can't see. Combine them, propagating W3C trace context so manual spans join the same traces. Semantic conventions give every service the same attribute names, so dashboards and queries work across the system; correlated traces, metrics and logs are what shorten incident response.
